contexts.text: A wall plastered with what is untempered () = what is fictitious appearing as truth.
There appeared walls, but no roof.
Like one who in the dark sees spots and streaks on a wall... AC 6400.
It appeared as if a wall were placed in the way; and when they attempted to overturn the wall, there rose up always a new wall. SE 993.
They appear... within a kind of wall. SE 1066.
There appeared to me a plaster-like wall, with sculpturing... (What it represented.)
When truth is spoken of... the walls of the rooms where they dwell sparkle with gold and silver.
The correspondence of the walls, etc. of the altar of incense.
Its walls () = the interiors; for walls, or sides, = interior things; for when the roof = the inmost, the walls, which are below, = the interior (or mediate) things. Explained.

The walls of their houses are as it were crystalline, thus transparent, and there appear in them as it were flowing forms which are representative of heavenly things, with perpetual variety. Explained.
A wall = truth in ultimates.
The building was divided into two by a transparent wall...
The wife appeared through the crystalline wall.
Many designs were on the walls (of the antechamber). Explained.
Such things are represented on these walls when in meditation about conjugial love...
The lights on the plastered walls presented images of birds of night. CL 380:4.
The walls on which the cherubim were carved () = the ultimates of Heaven and the Church. AE 458:3.

The wall round about, upon which they were seen painted () = the interiors everywhere in the natural man; for... the walls = the interior things (as distinguished from the inmost and the ultimate ones).
Who... leans with his hand upon the wall, and a serpent bites him () = that when such a one consults the Word in the sense of the letter... he does not see that evils are perverting it.

To bring out through the wall the vessels of migration, in the dark... () = that all the truths of doctrine from the Word had been cast out... The wall = the ultimate which encompasses and protects truths; and the ultimate of doctrine is the sense of the letter... which is called a wall because it contains and encloses the spiritual sense.
Men painted upon the wall () = (doctrinals which outwardly appear to be truths, although inwardly they are profane). A painted wall = the appearance of the doctrinal things in externals.
The wall out of which the stone crieth () = a man devoid of truths, and who consequently wishes to be instructed, from what is false.
The Spirits themselves can be passed into the houses through the walls...
